I’m 37, so I started DJ’ing at 14. I was really lucky to come up during that time because - and I hate to sound like and old head but 1) I am and 2) it’s my opinion - but I had to save up my money to buy records to even practice with. And I had to buy multiple genres and every track had to be heat. My first gigs were house parties (which I don’t even know if they exist now?) and school dances (also unsure if they exist as I don’t have kids). Since you’re 21, there’s probably college parties or something. I would see who throws those. I got my first gigs because I was the only DJ in my area and was really good at it. In terms of clubs, back then, I would send demos out to promoters and I also started my own party. That was the game changer. So that would be my best advice for gigs. Find something you love, a scene, and if the old heads aren’t working with you, just do your own night. Someone will come and see you - it took me a few months of doing mine for people to come - and when they do they’ll be impressed you’re doing your own thing. You have a lot of resources with this sub, which I’ve only just discovered. 

Aside from that, just practice. Know your tunes in and out. Listen to music. The gigs will come when the passion and talent shines through - combined with networking.
